reviews.title: TRIỆU NGỌC HÀ GIANG · IELTS 49 · W08 · Đề 1
reviews.overall: Bài đúng đề và đủ 164 từ. Em đã nêu được xu hướng tăng của chicken, xu hướng giảm của beef và lamb, cùng vị trí thấp nhất của fish. Cấu trúc “with a subsequent ...” và cách dùng “respectively” phù hợp. Tuy nhiên, mở bài thiếu giới từ và mạo từ; hai đoạn Detail chưa mô tả trọn diễn biến của beef và lamb, trong khi fish bị nhắc lại. Em cần chia lại hai đoạn theo bốn đối tượng, bổ sung mốc đầu và giữa cho beef, lamb, rồi soát mức tăng của chicken trước khi nộp lại.
reviews.dataGrouping: Đoạn đầu giới thiệu biểu đồ; đoạn hai là Overview, nêu xu hướng của ba loại thịt và thứ hạng cuối kỳ, nhưng chưa nói fish giảm nhẹ. Detail 1 mô tả trọn chicken rồi chỉ liệt kê mức cuối của beef, lamb, fish; Detail 2 chỉ trở lại với fish. Cô gợi ý giữ cách đi theo đối tượng em đã chọn: mô tả Chicken/Beef trong Detail 1, Lamb/Fish trong Detail 2, có mốc đầu, mốc giữa phù hợp và mốc cuối cho từng đường.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given line chart illustrates weekly consumption of fish and three types of meat a specific European nation over 25-year period commencing from 1979.
Overall, there was a significant increase in chicken consumption, while an opposite trend was observed in beef and lamb. Also of note is that chicken became the most consumed food by the end of the period, while fish consistently remained the lowest throughout the years.
To elaborate, in 1979, approximately 140 grams per person per week of chicken was consumed, with a subsequent considerable rise to nearly 200 grams in 1989 and a final, larger rise to 250 grams in 2004. In contrast, the figures for consumption of beef, lamb and fish all experienced declines, dropping to around 100 grams, 55 grams, and 40 grams respectively by the end of the period.
Regarding categories with lower data, fish consumption started at 60 grams in 1979, after which it experienced a decline before ending the period at 40 grams in 2004.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The given line chart illustrates weekly consumption of fish and three types of meat in a European country over a 25-year period commencing from 1979. The figures are measured in grams per person per week.

Overall, there was a significant increase in chicken consumption, while the opposite was true for beef and lamb. Beef had the highest figure initially, but chicken overtook it around 1989 and ranked first by 2004; fish remained the lowest and declined only slightly.

To elaborate, in 1979, approximately 140 grams per person per week of chicken was consumed, with a subsequent rise to nearly 200 grams in 1989 and a further rise to about 250 grams in 2004. In contrast, beef consumption began at roughly 220 grams, peaked at around 240 grams in the early 1980s, and then fell unevenly to about 100 grams by 2004.

Regarding lamb and fish, lamb consumption fell from about 150 grams in 1979 to around 100 grams in 1989, before ending the period at roughly 55 grams. Fish started at 60 grams and hovered around 40 to 50 grams for most years, ending at about 40 grams in 2004. Its decline was much smaller than that of lamb.

Overall, out of the studied nations, only France witnessed signs of a decline after reaching its peak. In addition, Italy emerged as the leader by the end of the period, overtaking Germany.

The line chart illustrates how female representation in parliament, measured as a percentage of all MPs, changed in Germany, Italy, France, the UK and Belgium between 2000 and 2012.

Overall, the proportion of female MPs rose in all five countries from the start to the end of the period, although France fell after peaking in 2004. Italy had the highest figure in 2012, while the UK, despite the largest overall increase, shared the lowest position with Belgium at that point.

To elaborate, in 2000, about 33% of MPs in Germany were women, compared with 26% in Italy and 25% in France. The German figure rose slightly to around 37% by 2012, whereas that for Italy climbed to nearly 39%, overtaking it. France's figure reached a peak of about 37% in 2004 before dropping to roughly 29% in 2008 and recovering to 31% in 2012.

Regarding the remaining countries, the proportion of female MPs in Belgium rose from 17% in 2000 to 28% in 2004, after which it remained relatively stable. The figure for the UK climbed more sharply from only 3% to 28% over the whole period, equalling that for Belgium in 2012.

The given pie chart illustrates the proportion of the primary reasons why individuals selected a speacific unuversity in the UK in two different years, between 1997 and 2007.
Overall, suitable degree courses remained the most popular reason for choosing the university in both years. Additionally, while the importance of distance to home and teaching quality grew, student interest in university resources and activities declined.
To elaborate, in 1997, suitable degree courses was the most popular factor, accounting for 35%, and this figure rose to 37% in 2007. The most dramatic increase was observed in proximity to parental home, which more than doubled from 10% to 22% over the decade. Similarly, the proportion of individuals the quality of teaching grew steadily from 15% to 18%.
Regarding the remaining, the percentage of students choosing a university based on its quality of resources fell from 21% to 17%. Additionally, the figure for sports and social activities witnessed a sharp decline, dropping from 19% to a mere 6% over the decade.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The two pie charts show how students' main reasons for choosing a particular university in the UK differed in 1997 and 2007. The figures are expressed as percentages of students.

Overall, the proportions choosing this university for suitable degree courses, proximity to their parental home and teaching quality increased, whereas the shares citing resources and sports and social activities fell. Suitable degree courses were the most common reason in both years. Proximity to parental home ranked last in 1997, while sports and social activities did so in 2007.

To elaborate, in 1997, 35% of students chose the university primarily for its suitable degree courses, and this figure rose slightly to 37% in 2007. The share citing proximity to their parental home more than doubled from 10% to 22%, the largest increase of any reason. Similarly, the figure for teaching quality increased from 15% to 18%.

Regarding the remaining reasons, the proportion of students choosing the university for the quality of its resources fell from 21% in 1997 to 17% in 2007. The figure for good sports and social activities declined more sharply, from 19% to 6%, making it the least common reason at the end of the period.
